comments.quote_zh: 如果你不同意，我向你发起挑战——看15分钟，然后贴出你的回复
comments.text_zh: 没有早点意识到超市肉类区是系统性、骇人地折磨有智慧生命的产物。像可能很多读到这段话的人一样，当我面对我们都隐约熟悉的丑恶事实时，我通常会感到有点愧疚。我用物种歧视的论点为自己的吃肉行为辩护（人类比猪、牛等等好太多了）。我妻子向我发起挑战，让我至少看一点那部纪录片；如果之后我还想吃萨拉米，那就吃吧。看完之后，我再也不想吃萨拉米了。我现在认为，食品工业代表无知的消费者对动物施加的极端虐待，很可能是21世纪最严重的恶行。如果你不同意，我向你发起挑战——看15分钟，然后贴出你的回复：[VIDEO]
comments.text: Not waking up earlier to the fact that the meat section in the supermarket is a product of systemic, gruesome torture of intelligent beings. Like probably many of you who read this, I usually felt a bit guilty when I was confronted with the ugly facts we are all vaguely familiar with. I justified my meat consumption with specieist arguments (humans are so much better than pigs, cows, etc). My wife challenged me to watch at least a little bit of a documentary, and if I still wanted to eat salami, so be it. Afterwards I didn't want to eat salami anymore. I now think that the extreme abuse of animals by the food industry on behalf of ignorant consumers is probably the worst evil of the 21st century. If you disagree, I challenge you - watch 15min and then post your reply: [VIDEO]

comments.why_zh: 纪录片展示了养殖中的动物被残害和屠宰。
comments.quote_zh: 看看 Dominion，然后告诉我们这些动物没有被残害、被撕裂、被折磨、被屠宰和被谋杀。
comments.text_zh: 那不是谋杀的完整定义。剩下的定义是：- 1：非法且怀有预谋恶意地杀死（一个人）- 2：肆意屠杀：SLAY - 3a：终结 - 3b：戏弄、折磨 - 3c：残害、撕裂 [VIDEO] 看看 Dominion，然后告诉我们这些动物没有被残害、被撕裂、被折磨、被屠宰和被谋杀。动物不想死。它们全都会自然而然地哭叫、尖叫、逃跑、反抗，并通常做任何可能的事来避免被杀。杀死它们就是谋杀。基于个体所属物种而对动物进行歧视或不公正对待，叫做物种歧视（Speciesism）。认为只有人类具有内在价值，或人类是宇宙中心实体的信念，叫做人类中心主义（Anthropocentrism）。
comments.text: That's not the full definition of murder. Here's the rest: - 1: to kill (a human being) unlawfully and with premeditated malice - 2: to slaughter wantonly : SLAY - 3a: to put an end to - 3b: TEASE, TORMENT - 3c: MUTILATE, MANGLE [VIDEO] Watch Dominion and tell us these animals are not being mutilated, mangled, tormented, slaughtered and murdered. Animals do not want to die. The will ALL naturally cry, scream, run, fight and generally do anything possible to avoid getting killed. Killing them is murder. Discrimination or unjustified treatment of animals based on an individual's species membership is called Speciesism. The belief that humans alone possess intrinsic value or are the central entity in the universe is called Anthropocentrism.

comments.story_title: Beyond Meat’s Beyond Burger life cycle assessment (2018)
comments.why_zh: 展示工厂化养殖场里真正发生的事。
comments.text_zh: 人类进化仍知之甚少，而“早期人类据称做出的任何选择 $X 导致了我们祖先异常快速的大脑发育”这一假设，完全是推测。 > 与如今大多数主要以植物为食的大型猿类不同，我们可以把前额叶皮层的发育归功于肉类惊人的营养密度，以及我们惊人的狩猎和制造工具能力。彻头彻尾的推测。 > 我们是群猎者，打造工具并制定能够猎杀猛犸象的策略。你想说这是“穷凶极恶”也行，但这不过是自然和生存。早期人类部落中的自给性狩猎，无论如何都不能与现代工厂化养殖相提并论。 B12 并非来自吃植物或动物：它来自细菌；讽刺的是，在工厂化养殖场里这种细菌如此匮乏，以至于动物需要注射合成 B12。 > 我个人认为，如果你哪怕稍微关心自己的健康，像 Beyond meat 这样的高度加工植物替代品都不是长期选择。我吃生大豆、豆类、谷物、坚果和种子。如果你关心自己的健康，我推荐看纪录片 Forks Over Knives [1]；如果你想看看工厂化养殖场里真正发生了什么，推荐看纪录片 Dominion [2]。 [1]: [LINK] [2]: [VIDEO]
comments.text: Human evolution is poorly understood, and the assumption that any choice $X supposedly made by early humans led to our forefathers’ anamolously rapid brain development is flatly speculative. > Unlike most great apes today, whose diet is primarily plant based, we can thank the incredible nutrient density in meat and our incredible hunting and tool creating ability for prefrontal cortex development. Complete and utter speculation. > We were pack hunters, forging tools and strategies capable of taking down mammoths. Call it 'diabolicaly evil' if you want, but this is simply nature and survival. Subsistence hunting amongst early human tribes is not comparable to modern day factory farming in any conceivable way. B12 doesn’t come from eating plants OR animals: it comes from bacteria, and ironically that bacteria is in such short supply on factory farms that the animals need to be injected with synthetic B12. > I don't personally believe highly processed plant alternatives such as Beyond meat are a long term option if you're even vaguely interested in your own health. I eat raw soybeans, legumes, grains, nuts and seeds. I’d recommend watching the documentary Forks Over Knives [1] if you care about your personal health, and the documentary Dominion [2], if you’d like to see what really happens on factory farms. [1]: [LINK] [2]: [VIDEO]

comments.text_zh: 如果你饲养并宰杀动物时，只需让它们承受现今养殖动物所承受痛苦的一小部分，那么吃肉基本没问题（也许除了环境问题）。不幸的是，除了极少数人——那些能自己饲养并宰杀动物，或有自己非常信任的人代劳的人——这对其他所有人都是不可能的。[0][1] 远超 95% 的肉来自工厂化养殖[2]，说得轻一点，在工厂化养殖场里饲养的动物生活得并不愉快。[3] 这话来自一个在农场长大、父母现在仍是农民的人。 [0] 人们以为从当地肉贩或当地农场购买，就一定能让肉合乎道德。事实上，与大型屠宰场相比，小型屠宰场的宰杀规程往往非常不靠谱。结果就是农民用棍棒把动物打死，或往猪头上打 5 枪才让它死掉：[LINK] [1] 狩猎并不是合乎道德的肉类来源。即便是职业猎人（例如在澳大利亚为农民猎杀袋鼠的人），也会让大约每 20 只中有 1 只带着子弹逃走。如果伤口凝血，但动物随后因内出血或感染而死去，这可能意味着数小时甚至数天的痛苦。我以前打猎，睡觉时还会想着那天受伤逃走的动物。尽管如此，我花了太久才意识到，根本没有必要吃动物。 [2] [LINK] [3] [VIDEO]
comments.text: If you could grow and kill with a small fraction of the suffering that farmed animals endure today, then eating meat would be mostly fine (other than environmental issues, perhaps). Unfortunately that's impossible for all but a very small minority of people - those who can raise and kill animals themselves or have someone they trust very well to do it for them.[0][1] Well over 95% of meat is factory farmed[2], and animals that are raised in factory farms do not live pleasant lives, to put it lightly.[3] This is coming from someone who grew up on a farm, and whose parents are still farmers. [0] People think that buying from their local butcher or local farm must make their meat ethical. In fact, small abbatoirs often have very shoddy killing protocols compared to the large ones. You end up with farmers clubbing animals to death, or putting 5 bullets into a pig's head before it dies: [LINK] [1] Hunting isn't an ethical source of meat. Even professional hunters (e.g. those who kill kangaroos for farmers in AU) will let ~1 in 20 get away with a bullet in them. That could mean suffering for hours or even days if it clots but then dies due to internal bleeding or infection. I used to hunt and I would go to sleep thinking about the animals that got away wounded that day. Still, it took me far too long to realise that there is no need to eat animals. [2] [LINK] [3] [VIDEO]

comments.why_zh: 营养讨论帖中的附带链接。
comments.text_zh: > 我吃它们是因为我不想不得不服用不受监管的补充剂，来弥补你只要吃肉就不会有的营养缺乏。B12 并不能可靠地从肉类中吸收。每个人都应该服用 B12 补充剂，除非他们吃 B12 强化麦片或定期做血液检查，但对大多数人来说补充剂是最便宜的方法。“对正在进行的 Framingham Offspring Study 中 3,000 名男女的仔细研究发现，39% 的人血浆 B12 水平处于‘低正常’范围——低于每升 258 皮摩尔。研究负责人 Katherine Tucker 说，虽然这远高于目前公认的缺乏水平 148 pmol/L，但有些人在较高范围就表现出神经系统症状……研究人员还预计会发现膳食摄入与血浆水平之间存在某种联系，尽管其他研究没有发现关联。他们确实发现了联系。补充剂的使用使处于危险区——血浆 B12 低于 185 pmol/L——的志愿者比例从 20% 降到 8%。每周吃五次或更多强化麦片，或乳制品摄入量位于最高三分之一，使处于该范围的志愿者比例降低了近一半——分别从 23% 和 24% 降至 12% 和 13%。奇怪的是，研究人员发现血浆 B12 水平与肉类、家禽和鱼类摄入之间没有关联，尽管这些食物提供了饮食中的大部分 B12。Tucker 说：‘这不是因为人们没有吃足够的肉。而是这种维生素没有被吸收。’”
comments.text: > i eat them bc i dont want to gave to take unregulated supplements to make up for nutrtional deficiencies you wouldnt have if you just ate meat. B12 isn’t reliably absorbed from meat. Everyone should be taking a b12 supplement unless they eat b12 fortified cereals or get regular blood work but supplements are the cheapest method for most. “ A careful look at 3,000 men and women in the ongoing Framingham Offspring Study found 39 percent with plasma B12 levels in the “low normal” range--below 258 picomoles per liter. While this is well above the currently accepted deficiency level of 148 pmol/L, some people exhibit neurological symptoms in the higher range, said study leader Katherine Tucker... The researchers also expected to find some connection between dietary intake and plasma levels, even though other studies found no association. And they did find a connection. Supplement use dropped the percentage of volunteers in the danger zone--plasma B12 below 185 pmol/L--from 20 percent to 8. Eating fortified cereals five or more times a week or being among the highest third for dairy intake reduced, by nearly half, the percentage of volunteers in that zone--from 23 and 24 percent, respectively, to 12 and 13 percent. Oddly, the researchers found no association between plasma B12 levels and meat, poultry, and fish intake, even though these foods supply the bulk of B12 in the diet. “It’s not because people aren’t eating enough meat,” Tucker said. “The vitamin isn’t getting absorbed.”

comments.story_title: Pamplona Bull Runs Reveal Dynamics of Crowds in Danger
comments.why_zh: 被引作工厂化养殖中存在痛苦的证据。
comments.quote_zh: 工厂化养殖客观上是这颗星球有史以来最大的痛苦生产者
comments.text_zh: 就为了娱乐而伤害动物而言，我们可以从自己的餐食中找灵感。普通人因其饮食选择造成的痛苦，将比奔牛节多出几个数量级。工厂化养殖客观上是这颗星球有史以来最大的痛苦生产者 [1, 2]，而大多数人消费它们生产的肉是为了享乐，而非必需。[1]: [VIDEO] [2]: [LINK]
comments.text: As far as hurting animals for entertainment goes, we can look at our meals for inspiration. The average person will cause magnitudes more suffering than the bull runs thanks to their dietary choices. Factory farms are objectively the largest producers of suffering this planet has ever seen [1, 2], and most people consume the meat they produce for pleasure as opposed to necessity. [1]: [VIDEO] [2]: [LINK]

comments.story_title: Wild orangutan seen healing his wound with a plant
comments.why_zh: 以脚注形式引作养殖中动物被折磨的证据。
comments.text_zh: > 我们吃肉。纯粹为了口味。 > 我们需要吃肉。错。世界上10-20%的人不吃肉，我们也过得很好。 > 所以我们需要为此杀死动物。不，你想杀动物是因为你想要好吃的食物。不是因为你“需要”肉。生活在工业化国家的人没人需要。制作植物性均衡饮食（而且还很好吃）轻而易举。 > 动物园绝对不是人类生存所必需的。工厂化养殖场也不是。它们的存在是为了满足“味蕾嗡嗡叫”。但这不值得把一只动物活活折磨[1]致死。 [1]: [VIDEO]
comments.text: > We eat meat. Purely for taste. > We need to eat meat. False. 10-20% of the world population does not and we're just fine. > So we need to kill animals for that. No, you want to kill animals because you want tasty food. Not because you "need" meat. No one living in an industrialized country does. It's trivial to create a plant-based balanced diet (and a tasty one at that.) > Zoos absolutely not required for humans to survive. Neither are factory farms. They exist to satisfy "taste buds go brr." But that is not worth literally torturing[1] an animal to death. [1]: [VIDEO]
